result.rationale: The migration does interpolate host values directly into SQL: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` — the values come from the old site_setting and may contain http:// prefixes, CRLF (from a host_list textarea), or quotes, none of which are sanitized. Unlike the model (which strips http:// in before_validation), migration-inserted rows bypass that. record_for_host queries lower(host) = uri.host, so a stored 'http://example.com' never matches 'example.com'. Verifiable from the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration copies legacy SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts into the new table via raw SQL string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. This both (a) can break or be exploited if `h` contains a single quote (no escaping/quoting) and (b) bypasses the EmbeddableHost `before_validation` normalization (stripping `http(s)://` and paths) because it’s not using the model layer. As a result, scheme-prefixed entries (and entries with trailing whitespace/CR like `\r`) can be stored unnormalized and then fail later lookups in `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` which compares `lower(host)` to the parsed URI host.
